clue.text: Attendant carrying too much soup

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: a page is a young attendant or servant
OTT abbreviates over the top, meaning excessive

explanation.surface: A waiter is bringing far more soup than anyone ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attendant carrying' reads as a waiter with a tray, but the attendant is the outer word holding the excess inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottage is an old word for a thick vegetable stew or broth, a kind of soup.

clue.text: Relative very irate at first with cat in Oval building?

indicators.note: at first points to beginnings, so only opening letters are kept

blocks.note: pa is a father, a relative
the opening letters of the two words
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A furious relative arrives with a cat at an oval-shaped building.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground; its pavilion is the clubhouse where players change, and the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket pavilion is the main clubhouse at a ground, so one stands at the Oval.

clue.text: Endures taster Leo prepared

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked on and made ready, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A food taster called Leo puts up with whatever has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' sounds like cooking, matching the taster, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure something is to put up with it, the same sense as tolerate.

clue.text: One who assists attacker without shelter

indicators.note: a shelter is an outer covering, so stripping it off leaves only the inside letters

blocks.note: a raider is an attacker; its outer letters are stripped

explanation.surface: A helper of an attacker is left without a roof over their head.
explanation.walkthrough: The attacker is RAIDER; losing its outer R at each end leaves the helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant or helper, especially to someone senior.

clue.text: Pass old soldiers occupying centre of Gretna Green?

indicators.note: to occupy is to fill a space, so pieces go inside another
centre points to the middle, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
O is the abbreviation for old
GIs are American soldiers
the middle two letters of the six

explanation.surface: Veterans holding a mountain pass near Gretna Green in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green is a Scottish village famous for runaway weddings; the surface reads it as one place, but 'Green?' is the definition, a question mark marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green is an environmental campaigner, and an ecologist studies or protects the natural environment.

clue.text: Carpet at the end enthralling American doctor

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold someone captive, so one piece holds others captive within it

blocks.note: last means at the end
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
A is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A rug left lying at the end of the room captivates a visiting American physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is a verb here, as in to carpet someone, meaning to give them a dressing-down; the doctor and the American sit inside in the order MB then A.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for reprimanding them severely, and to lambast is to criticise harshly.

clue.text: City blazes a trail according to reporter

indicators.note: a reporter's words reach us spoken, so the clue is taken by sound

blocks.note: to blaze a trail is to go first and show the way

explanation.surface: A city is described by a journalist as pioneering.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major city in West Yorkshire, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Spread stuff about a lot of illness on base

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters run the other way
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to ram is to stuff or cram
a malady is an illness
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Smearing something about with plenty of disease on a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb with 'stuff' its object, but it is the noun for something on toast; e is the mathematical constant used as the base of natural logs.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve that is spread on toast, so it is a spread.

clue.text: Article covers styling product for Guardian?

indicators.note: a cover wraps round something, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article
hair gel is a styling product

explanation.surface: A newspaper article reviews a hair product for The Guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Guardian as the newspaper; the question mark shows it is a guardian angel, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is a protective spirit, so an angel can be thought of as a guardian.

clue.text: Fools stow beer periodically outside of pubs

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
the outside of a word is its edge, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: the even letters of the two words
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Idiots occasionally stash their beer outside the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are lifted straight from the clue's words, alternate letters first and then the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or foolish person, so twerps are fools.

clue.text: Love cycling back to grand capital stadium

indicators.note: cycling means going round a loop, so letters move from the front round to the back
the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written before its letters are cycled
the final letter of the word
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A cycling enthusiast returns to a grand stadium in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' looks like G or K for a thousand, but 'back to' asks only for its last letter; LOVE with its L cycled to the end becomes VELO.
explanation.definitionFit: A velodrome is an arena with a banked track built for cycle racing, so it is a type of stadium.

clue.text: Crook in make-up you heard moving east

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling
east is rightwards in an across entry, so one letter shifts to a later slot in the word

blocks.note: rouge is red cosmetic powder for the cheeks
the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: A villain disguised in theatrical make-up, travelling eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the cosmetic and shift its U one place to the right, past the G; the U is the 'you heard' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or unprincipled person, which is the slang sense of crook.

clue.text: Fat poet having left for Belgium

indicators.note: one thing put in place of another, so one letter is swapped in where the other stood

blocks.note: a bard is a poet
L is the abbreviation for left
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: An overweight poet has quit his post and moved to Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having left for Belgium' reads as emigration; it means L takes the place of B.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking, so it is a kind of fat.

clue.text: Rubbish detective by barrier inside supermarket

indicators.note: something inside is held within another, so pieces go within an outer word

blocks.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant
a wall is a barrier
the Co-op is a British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A store detective lurking by a barrier inside a supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British cooperative supermarket chain; the detective and the barrier sit together inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Codswallop is British slang for nonsense, the sense of rubbish meaning foolish talk.

clue.text: Exile over by street facing discrimination

blocks.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
St is the abbreviation for street
racism is discrimination by race

explanation.surface: A man forced out of his street faces prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, written O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism is exclusion from a group, which is a social form of exile or banishment.

clue.text: Purple and gold cap almost sealing drink

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
to seal is to close round something, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a beret is a soft cap
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A purple and gold cap nearly covering a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purple and gold' reads as a colour scheme, but only 'Purple' is the definition; BERET loses its T before closing round the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine is a dark purple colour named after the vegetable, so it is a shade of purple.

clue.text: Heavy delivery of shellfish north of isle

indicators.note: a speaker's delivery is how words are spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a mussel is a shellfish
the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A large consignment of seafood is sent to somewhere north of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'north of' puts the first piece above the second; 'Heavy' is the noun for a hired tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy is slang for a big, strong thug or bodyguard, which is what a muscleman is.

clue.text: Total of five hundred after promotion

blocks.note: an ad, an advert, is a promotion
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A salary total of five hundred after someone gets promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests a rise at work, but it is advertising; 'after' places the numeral second.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures is to add them up, both verbs meaning to find a sum.

clue.text: Spotted object on land storing the Spanish fuel

indicators.note: to store is to keep something inside, so one piece is held in another

blocks.note: a die is a cube marked with spots
soil is land or ground
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Something spotted lying on land where Spanish fuel is stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'seen', but it means marked with spots, as a die is.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel oil is the heavy petroleum fuel burned in diesel engines.

clue.text: Sweatier in action so to speak

indicators.note: something in action is moving about, so the letters are set in motion into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone getting sweatier when active, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In action' sounds like exercise to match the sweat, but it is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were and so to speak are both phrases flagging that words are used loosely or figuratively.

clue.text: Vehicle kept back in reserve

indicators.note: back means backwards here, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A spare vehicle is held back in reserve at the depot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept back' sounds like holding something in reserve, which suits the surface, but it turns the vehicle round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub, short for substitute, is a reserve player who waits on the bench.

clue.text: Vulgar son visiting gallery with two thirds of class

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one piece enters another
only part of the word is wanted, so a third of its letters are dropped

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the Tate is a London art gallery
a lesson is a class at school

explanation.surface: A crude boy visits an art gallery with most of his school class.
explanation.walkthrough: LESSON has six letters, so two thirds of it is its first four.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar and tasteless both describe something crude, lacking refinement or good judgement.

clue.text: Excite core of groupies at bottom of prison

indicators.note: the core is the middle, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: stir is slang for prison
the two central letters of eight

explanation.surface: Groupies cause excitement at the bottom of a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'at bottom of' puts the core below the prison; stir is old slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up feelings or a crowd is to excite or rouse them.

clue.text: Celebrant wandering around a place of worship

indicators.note: something wandering has no fixed course, so the letters stray into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest strolls around a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, but it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a building or tent used for worship, notably in nonconformist and Jewish tradition.

clue.text: Flier avoiding current shift

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep away from it, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: a budgie is a bird, a flier
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A pilot steers clear of a shift in air currents.
explanation.walkthrough: A budgie, short for budgerigar, is a small pet parrot; I stands for current in physics formulae.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to move slightly, so it means to shift position.

clue.text: Last month, artist from the south made a bow

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming from the south means reading upward, the opposite way

blocks.note: Dec is December, the last month
an RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Last month an artist from the south took a bow on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a bow' suggests a stage bow; it means formed a curve, the bow of an archer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow is a curve, so to make a bow is to bend in a curve, or arc.

clue.text: Student might take this flower

blocks.note: first meaning: an exam a pupil sits
second meaning: something that flows, a river in Hampshire

explanation.surface: A student picking a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a flower is often a river, something that flows; the Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is an examination set for students, and the Test is the name of an English river.

clue.text: Vault tense with no storage space

blocks.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
O, zero, is nothing
MB, megabyte, is a unit of computer storage

explanation.surface: A nervous gymnast about to vault, with no room to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests a gymnastic leap, but it is the noun for a burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is an underground burial chamber, which is a kind of tomb.

clue.text: Exposed X-ray finally identified two bones

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go and the inside stays
finally points to the very end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: the word with its outer letters stripped
the last letter of the word
II is the Roman numeral for 2

explanation.surface: An X-ray film finally shows a pair of broken bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' fits a photographic film, but here it strips X and Y from XRAY; 'two' looks like part of the definition but is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone, and radii is its plural, the Latin form for more than one.

clue.text: Company further involving MOD officer

indicators.note: to involve is to take in or include, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
more means further or additional
taken as written: the Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: A company gets more deeply involved with a Ministry of Defence official.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence, lifted here as its letters unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A commodore is a senior naval rank above captain, so it is a commissioned officer.

clue.text: Sham figure put in power by socialist

indicators.note: to put one thing in another is to place it inside, so a piece is inserted

blocks.note: ten is a number, a figure
P is the symbol for power in physics
a red is a left-winger or socialist

explanation.surface: A puppet leader is installed in power by a left-wing party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sham figure' reads as a figurehead, but 'figure' belongs to the wordplay as a number, placed inside P plus RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sham and pretend are both adjectives for something fake or make-believe, not genuine.

clue.text: Astronomical features from North Derby uploaded regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for North
the second, fourth and every other letter after

explanation.surface: Telescope images of space from a North Derby observatory are posted online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uploaded' tempts a down-style reversal, but it is only fodder: take the even letters of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are clouds of gas and dust in space, objects astronomers observe.
